source.title_on_document: EXPLORING THE IMPACT OF GENERATIVE STIMULI ON THE CREATIVITY OF DESIGNERS IN COMBINATIONAL DESIGN

paper_design_summary: Twenty design students worked remotely on two 10-minute hand-sketch tasks (bike combined with horse, headphone combined with arch). Each person got one image stimulus (a Google image of the horse or the arch) for one task and one generative stimulus (a StyleGAN2 image that fuses the two concepts, made by the researchers) for the other. After the tasks, each person chose which stimulus worked better on novelty, smoothness, and usefulness. No one scored the sketches.

studies.label: Combinational design sketching with generative versus image stimuli

assignment.what_was_assigned: Which stimulus combination each participant got (Stimuli A+D or Stimuli B+C), so which task each person did with the generative stimulus and which with the image stimulus. Every participant used both stimulus types.
assignment.quote: Next, a combination of stimuli (Stimuli A+D or Stimuli B+C) was chosen as the experimental material, and it was ensured that a similar number of participants received each combination.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 1810), Section 3.4 Experiment design

arms.name: Generative stimuli
arms.description: GAN-fused image of target product and combinational object (Stimuli B: horse-bike; Stimuli D: arch-headphone)

arms.name: Image stimuli
arms.description: Google image of the combinational object (Stimuli A: horse; Stimuli C: stone arch)

participants.who: 20 participants with design education and/or design work experience, aged 21-30, 5 male and 15 female; 9 undergraduate students and 11 postgraduates; backgrounds product/industrial (11), UI/UX (6), graphic (2), jewellery (1). Within-person design, so the same 20 people are in both arms; the paper does not give how many got each stimulus combination.
participants.quote: As shown in Table 1, 20 participants with backgrounds in design education and/or design working experience were invited to conduct the experiment.
participants.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 1809), Section 3.2 Participants and Table 1; n=20 also in the abstract (PDF p. 1) and Conclusion (PDF p. 8)

ai_tool.name_model: StyleGAN2 generative adversarial networks trained by the researchers on 2500 bike images and 2300 headphone images; fused images made by projecting the horse/arch image into the latent space and moving toward a product vector (not prompt-based)

task.description: Two combinational design tasks, each producing one hand sketch: a bike combined with a horse and a headphone combined with a stone arch

outcomes.name: Self-reported preference: which stimulus brought more novelty
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Novelty: Generative Stimuli 11 (55%) vs Image Stimuli 9 (45%) of 20 participants

outcomes.name: Self-reported preference: which stimulus gave a smoother ideation process
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Smoothness: Generative Stimuli 16 (80%) vs Image Stimuli 4 (20%) of 20 participants

outcomes.name: Self-reported preference: which stimulus brought more usefulness
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Usefulness: Generative Stimuli 12 (60%) vs Image Stimuli 8 (40%) of 20 participants

eligibility.reason: Criterion 2: 20 people analyzed (PDF p. 5, Section 3.2 and Table 1), far below 50. Criterion 1: within-person design in which every participant used both stimuli; the paper says only that a similar number of participants received each stimulus combination and does not say the allocation or order was random (PDF p. 6, Section 3.4); the stimuli are researcher-made StyleGAN2 images, not output of a prompt-based generative AI tool. Criterion 3: the only outcomes are participants' self-reported choice of the better stimulus; the paper states that the evaluation of creativity comes from the designers themselves (PDF p. 5, Section 3.3), and no rater or computed measure scores the sketches. The triage count of fewer than 50 participants is confirmed.

one_line_finding: Of 20 designers, 11 (55%) chose the GAN-generated stimulus over the image stimulus for novelty, 16 (80%) for smoothness, and 12 (60%) for usefulness, all self-reported preferences with no scoring of the sketches (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1810, Table 2).
